text:
ara: Quick profile from the canary this morning — we hit OOM-like failures during 90th pct tail when concurrent small-chat and long-context requests interleave. looks like the kernel chooser prefers the fast-fused kernel but it blows the KV footprint in those mixed loads.

sam: Can you paste the top-line numbers? memory usage / KV growth / batch sizes?

ara: 1) baseline single request KV: ~120MB. 2) when a 512-token chat enters a batch dominated by many 8-token requests, batch token budget spikes and KV checkpoint climbs to ~1.1GB within 200ms. 3) kernel selection logs show 'fused_attn_v2' chosen 87% of the time.

leila: Interesting — so fused kernel gives throughput but allocs larger temporary buffers that don't play nice with KV. Do we have metric correlating kernel_choice -> ephemeral_allocs?

ara: yes, added a quick trace: 
```
kernel_choice=fused_attn_v2 ephemeral_alloc=820MB kv_reserved=320MB total_gpu=12GB
kernel_choice=light_attn_pack ephemeral_alloc=180MB kv_reserved=320MB total_gpu=12GB
```

jordan: Suggestion: add a kernel-fit penalty when KV_reserve + ephemeral_alloc > soft_kv_threshold (we already compute that threshold per-GPU). penalty should bias towards light_attn_pack or the quantized path for mixed batches.

sam: We should also look at batch formation heuristics — right now admission only cares about token_budget and latency SLO, not the ephemeral memory footprint. If we add a cost function that approximates ephemeral_alloc per-kernel per-token we can prefer smaller kernels for batch candidates.

leila: Agreed. Proposal: when queueing, compute a "projected transient usage" = sum(existing_kv_reserved + kernel_ephe_per_token * candidate_tokens). Reject candidate or route to slow-path if projected transient > kv_soft_headroom. Slow-path = isolated single-request batch or fallback kernel.

ara: Implementation detail: we can get kernel_ephe_per_token from profiling table (we already have a csv per-model/kernel/seqlen). small overhead to look up. We also need a cheap estimator for multi-request mixing costs (worst-case ordering).

jordan: For ordering, use conservative additive model but allow a 10% slack when traffic is homogeneous. Also add a preemptive admission gate: if current kv_reserved > high_water and incoming request tokens > X, force it into the quarantine queue (single-batch path).

sam: Quarantine queue sounds good but watch for latency churn. Maybe instead of single-request we use micro-batches with light kernel only. That keeps throughput while bounding transient allocs.

leila: Also add an eviction hint: if batch formation would cause soft headroom breach, attempt a fast KV soft-evict of least-recent prefixes (best-effort) before admitting. If eviction completes within Y ms allow admission; otherwise route to fallback. This avoids rejecting legitimate traffic.

ara: FYI I ran a quick sim on a traffic trace. With kernel-penalty + projected-transient gating, 99th pct OOM events dropped from 7 -> 1 per hour on the canary. Micro-batch fallback kept p95 latency within SLO.

jordan: Nice. Next steps: 1) add kernel_ephe lookup in admission path (low-cost cache), 2) implement projected_transient check + quarantine route, 3) add soft-evict hook and metric. I'll draft an RFC.

sam: Also add an observability column: kernel_choice, projected_transient, admission_decision, kv_reserved_pre/post, eviction_attempted. Want to be able to reproduce.

leila: I'll own the profiling sweep to fill kernel_ephe table for all models on the fleet (will run overnight).

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled: admission-gate-v0.1 -> eng-runtime/canary at 08:30 UTC.

ara: Thanks — I'll follow the canary and post early signals (OOM count, p95 tail, eviction ops).

sam: Sounds good. If we see regressions we can toggle kernel_penalty off remotely.

jordan: RFC in #eng-runtime docs by EOD. tagging infra to reserve canary nodes.

leila: one more note — add a machine-level env var to disable ephemeral pre-allocations in fused kernels until we have robust gating. That gives immediate relief on clusters with tight KV requirements.

ara: true, will add flag to fused kernel launch config.

sam: Great. Thanks everyone.
